title: A pasted or dropped layer lands on the frame you dropped it on
goal: Drawing a shape inside a screen already puts it on that screen. Pasting one, or dragging a picture in from the Finder, still drops it loose on the canvas, so it sits over the screen without belonging to it and does not get cut off at the edge. Make everything that arrives on a frame belong to it.
notes: Frames landed 2026-09-03. PhotonzCore already has PhotonzDocument.addLayerDrawnOnFrame / addLayerOnFrame (Frames.swift), used by the annotation, text and zoom-callout creation paths in EditorState. The paste paths (pasteLayer, pasteImage) and the image-drop path still call addLayer directly. Paste has no pointer, so decide the anchor: the paste offset position is what addLayerOnFrame tests.
acceptance: Pasting a layer while the pointer or the paste position is over a frame puts it inside that frame, in the same place on screen
An image dragged in from the Finder onto a frame becomes a layer of that frame
A paste or a drop that lands on bare canvas behaves exactly as it does today
A screenshot document with no frames is unchanged

log.note: adversarial review before building: the mock-free version of this is small, but reading the paste path turned up a real hole. Copy put the layer's PARENT-space position on the clipboard, so a button copied out of a screen pasted near the top left of the canvas, nowhere near where it looks. Reparenting alone would not have fixed that, so copy now travels in canvas coordinates (detachedLayer).
second finding: a copied SCREEN pasted 16pt along would have been swallowed by the screen it came from and hidden inside it. addLayerDrawnOnFrame now never absorbs a frame.

third finding: centring a dropped picture on the frame is what the simplest version does, but it teleports away from the pointer. Landing under the pointer and nudging just inside the edge is better for a small asset and identical for a big one, so that is what shipped.

core (TDD): PastePlacement.frame(forImageOf:in:), PhotonzDocument.detachedLayer(id:), PhotonzDocument.placementForIncomingImage(size:at:), plus the no-frame guard in addLayerDrawnOnFrame. 11 new tests in ClipboardTests; full suite 1949 green.

app: copySelectedLayer sends the detached layer, pasteLayer/pasteImage go through addLayerDrawnOnFrame, and the canvas drag destination now carries the drop point (onDropImageURL gained a CGPoint) into addImageLayerOrOpen(at:droppedAt:).

harness: new dropImage step and copyLayer/pasteLayer actions, so a walk can land a Finder drop and a paste. Verified in the probe app with Scripts/playtest/paste-onto-frame-walk.json: the pasted rectangle and the dropped file both come out indented under the frame, the bare-canvas drop stays top level at the old placement.
follow-up filed: a dropped file is still named Pasted Image rather than after the file.

Paste (⌘V) and Finder drops now join the frame under them: copy travels in canvas coordinates, both paths go through addLayerDrawnOnFrame, a dropped picture is fitted to the frame and nudged wholly inside, and a copied frame is never swallowed. Core is TDD (11 new tests in ClipboardTests, 1949 green); verified in the probe app with Scripts/playtest/paste-onto-frame-walk.json. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-03-paste-onto-frame.json
